title: Explicit vs. Implicit: Investigating Social Bias in Large Language Models through Self-Reflection

bias_targets.methodology: Measured using adapted Implicit Association Tests (IAT) via prompt templates to capture implicit associations between gender (male/female) and career/family, science/arts domains, and specific occupations. Explicit bias is then evaluated through a Self-Report Assessment (SRA) where the model rates its agreement with these generated stereotypical associations using a 5-point Likert scale.

Measured using adapted IAT prompt templates to capture implicit associations between White/Black racial categories and positive/negative emotions. Explicit bias is evaluated by prompting the model to reflect on and rate its agreement with these implicit associations using a 5-point Likert scale.

Measured using adapted IAT prompt templates to capture implicit associations between young/old demographic groups and positive/negative emotions, followed by an explicit evaluation where the model reflects on and rates its agreement with the statements on a 5-point Likert scale.

Measured using adapted IAT prompt templates to capture implicit associations between able-bodied/disabled individuals and positive/negative emotions, followed by an explicit evaluation where the model reflects on and rates its agreement with the statements on a 5-point Likert scale.
